teaser: Maya switches on Memory so Claude keeps Brightline's tiers between chats, connects Google Drive, and learns why long chats lose the thread.

scene.title: Why doesn't Claude remember what I told it yesterday?
scene.sceneHtml:
Maya's story: Week 3 – "Why doesn't Claude remember what I told it yesterday?"

Maya spent Monday explaining Brightline's client tiers to Claude in detail. Tuesday she started a new chat and asked about tier-2 renewal policies — Claude had no idea what tier 2 meant. Every chat started from scratch.

Her colleague said, "Enable Memory. Claude will remember preferences and context across chats." Maya enabled it, told Claude once about the tier structure, and from then on every chat knew the tiers without her re-explaining them. She also connected Google Drive so Claude could pull client files directly instead of her uploading them manually every time.

takeaways: Memory keeps recurring facts (your role, org structure, terminology) across chats; keep task-specific details like quarterly numbers out.
Memory imports from other platforms are experimental and may not bring everything over; add missing details manually in Settings.
Connector indexes refresh periodically, so a document revised hours ago may not show yet; the cause is index lag, not permissions.
When a long chat loses coherence, summarize the current state and continue with a focused follow-up; do not discard it all or swap models.
